title.narrative: Emergency floods response in Picos, Piaui

description.narrative:
This 6 month emergency response project aims to support 200 families from four communities who were affected by floods in January 2025, in the municipality of Picos, Piaui state. The project has two aims: a) To distribute multi-purpose cash cards to 200 families with R$ 200 per month, for 3 months (totalling £86 per family for three months), to contribute to their post-emergency needs, such as: building materials such as paints, electrical and plumbing equipment, food, cleaning materials and sleeping materials such as hammocks and sheets. b) To support four communities to monitor public funding which has been earmarked by the federal government to recover the social and structural damage caused by the heavy rains, so that the funds reach communities that are most critically in need of post-emergency rebuilding.
The municipality of Picos, in Piauí, is facing one of the worst situations in the last 30 years, caused by the heavy rains that occurred on 13 - 14th January 2025. According to the state's Environment Secretariat, on the night of 13 January, it rained around 135 millimetres in three hours, affecting at least 500 families, including 50 homeless people and two deaths. With several neighbourhoods flooded, the Fire Brigade rescued victims who were trapped in their homes, some on top of roofs or furniture.
The state decreed a state of public emergency on 14th January 2025, which was recognised by the federal government on the 18th January, making it possible for the municipality to present a work plan for the allocation of R$ 3 million (£429k) by the federal government. However, so far Caritas has not had access to the work plan for the use of these funds as it has not yet been made available on the government's digital platforms for public access. This will be the focus on Caritas' advocacy and mobilisation actions in this project.
